image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) standing on a paved surface in front of a red brick wall. The duck on the left is viewed from the rear/side, displaying its grey body, white tail feathers, and orange webbed feet. The duck on the right is facing forward/right, showing its characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, brown chest, and grey body. Both appear to be walking or standing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck on the right clearly displays a broad, flat, yellowish-green bill typical of a mallard drake.
The visible eye of the right duck is small and dark, consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit the classic robust, oval-shaped body structure of a mallard with smooth, dense-looking feather texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck on the right perfectly matches the male mallard description: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, brown chest, and grey flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs are bright orange and positioned posteriorly. The feet are clearly webbed with visible toe structures, appearing anatomically correct for a waterfowl.
The folded wings on the left duck show the correct layered structure and shape, tucked neatly against the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left duck displays the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (sex feathers), a definitive trait of mature drakes.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drakes) and rule out hybrid or generic 'duck' classifications.
To verify the structural integrity of the legs and feet, ensuring no fusion or extra limbs, which are common AI artifacts in waterfowl.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex feather textures and the background, and ensure individual feathers don't melt into each other.
To assess overall sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle texture anomalies in the pavement or brickwork.

focus_areas: Webbed foot anatomy (toe count and webbing connectivity)
Feather texture consistency (especially at the wing edges)
Boundary sharpness between the green head and the brick background
Symmetry and proportion of the two subjects
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the feet of both ducks. AI often struggles with the specific geometry of webbed feet on hard surfaces. Verify if the shadows under the feet match the lighting direction. Check if the 'curl' of the tail feathers on the left duck looks physically plausible or like a texture glitch.
